title: Unified SDK auth patterns: ephemeral refresh, rotation UX, and streaming reauth ergonomics
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Define and implement consistent auth patterns for Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs focused on: 1) short-lived (ephemeral) credentials and safe local dev UX, 2) key rotation flows with minimal developer friction, and 3) streaming-friendly reauth that preserves in-flight streams without data loss. Deliverables: design RFC, cross-language reference implementations, integration tests, and docs/examples for migrating enterprise customers from long-lived API keys to SSO/ephemeral models.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs offer a background credential refresher with retry/backoff that is enabled by default for SSO tokens and configurable for API key-derived ephemeral tokens. 2) Streaming call surface (streaming.generate / chat.stream) automatically reauthenticates on 401 without dropping persisted client-side event handlers; reconnects should resume where possible. 3) Key rotation example + migration guide published for Python/TS/Go. 4) Security review completed and release notes include migration steps.

design_decisions: - Use short-lived tokens by default for SSO in all SDKs (recommended TTL 15m). - Expose a pluggable TokenProvider interface: SDKs ship a default that talks to the environment (env var, file, or SSO callback) and a refresh-capable implementation that transparently rotates tokens. - Background refresh is per-process when possible, with per-client fallback. - Streaming reauth strategy: on 401 during streaming, attempt one immediate refresh+resume if refresh succeeds; otherwise surface an error and provide an automatic reconnect/backoff loop configurable by the app. - For API key rotation, provide helper CLI + programmatic tool for rotating keys with a 'dual-keys' overlap period and a small outage-free window using ephemeral pre-signed tokens for inbound requests.
implementation_notes: Key components to implement across Python/TS/Go: 1) TokenProvider interface + default implementations (env, file, SSO exchange). 2) BackgroundRefresher: jittered exponential backoff, max retries, pluggable backoff strategy. 3) StreamAuthMiddleware: handles injection of Authorization metadata on stream open; on 401 attempts refresh+resume. 4) CLI helper 'rw-sdk rotate-keys' (alpha) to do staged key rollouts using the platform's rotate endpoint. 5) Telemetry hooks: emit non-sensitive events: token_refresh.success, token_refresh.failure, streaming.reauth.attempt, streaming.reauth.success, streaming.reauth.failure.
streaming_reauth_sequence: 1) Client opens streaming connection with current auth header. 2) Server returns 401 or special reauth frame when token expired. 3) SDK's StreamAuthMiddleware pauses delivery to user handlers, triggers TokenProvider.refresh(). 4) If refresh succeeds within configured window (default 5s), middleware reopens stream or resumes via existing websocket/session resume token. 5) If refresh fails, middleware retries with exponential backoff (configurable attempts) and then invokes user-level error callback with guidance to re-create client. Note: for gRPC we prefer per-call metadata refresh; for websocket we use resume ids when available.
recommended_rotation_policy: - Enterprise: rotate primary API keys every 90 days, short-lived SSO tokens (15m TTL) with refreshable sessions. - Public SDKs: encourage SSO and ephemeral tokens; document how to keep dev productivity (local cred helper that issues ephemeral creds from SSO). - Provide sample `rotate_keys.py`/`rotate_keys.ts` that demonstrates: create new key, gradually update services to accept new key, mark old key for revoke after 24h overlap, and revoke old key programmatically.
security_considerations: - Never log tokens or full auth headers. Telemetry must only include token refresh outcomes and non-sensitive metadata. - Default SDKs should prefer refreshable short-lived tokens over long-lived keys. - Provide secure local dev helper that stores ephemeral creds in OS keyring (macOS Keychain / Windows Credential Manager / Linux libsecret) instead of plaintext files. - On rotation, the SDK should surface an explicit 'rotation_in_progress' event so apps can choose to drain or fail fast depending on criticality.
qa_plan: 1) Unit tests for TokenProvider implementations and Backoff logic. 2) Integration tests: simulated auth server that issues tokens + revoke endpoints; verify streaming reauth recovers in <5s in at least 95% of cases. 3) Load test in staging with 10k short-lived token refreshes/hour to validate token service scaling. 4) Manual UX walkthrough and docs review with Developer Experience team.
notes: Avoid per-request heavyweight locks in high-throughput server apps. Prefer a fast in-memory token lookup with a background nullable refresh to reduce tail latency. We'll validate by running the SDKs against canary workloads and collecting token refresh latency percentiles.
